before.text: Before any product slice depends on a device, provider, feed, lineup or voice route, the program shall run the spike for that route on the real target and land `spikes/<sp>/VERDICT.md` stating the verdict, the exact route tried, the observed result with evidence paths, the conditional it triggers (C1, C2, C5, C6, C8) and the register UIDs it unblocks.

The panel-beside-provider-video spike shall return its verdict within spike_panel_max of the first app install on the stick (recorded by P2-X01), and the verdict shall select `PanelMode.modeB` only with on-device evidence of simultaneous provider video and panel with no overlap or crop; otherwise it shall select `PanelMode.fullScreen` (AFC-PR-047).

The provider-link spike shall try Prime Video (TNF), ESPN app, DirecTV Stream app and YouTube TV in that order plus local-broadcast channel display, and shall record for each provider the package identity, the supported launch URI or intent with its documentation source, the observed routing outcome from the six-value vocabulary, and whether game arrival was observed; it shall invent no URI format.

The gate entrypoint `tools/ci/gate.sh` shall gain the areas `tvapp` (Gradle unit tests, Android lint and debug assemble under `tv-app/`) and `backend` (pytest and SAM template validation under `backend/`), invoked by the same local hooks and Actions workflow with path filters, stable check names and pinned actions per AC-AFC-CI-02; each area shall exit non-zero on any failing check, shall record a missing tool as a typed gap with its exact error and exit non-zero, and shall report `PASS` with the detail `no <dir>/ tree` only when its directory does not exist.
before.Source: DEC-AFC-SD-023 (Phase 2 adds product areas), Phase 1 AC-AFC-CI-01/02, CONTRACT-AFC-GATE

before.text: The Vnv guidance tree shall gain `docs/vnv/tv-app/AGENTS.md`, `docs/vnv/backend/AGENTS.md` and `docs/vnv/device-integration/AGENTS.md`, each naming Scope, Tools, Review Focus and findings target, and the index `docs/vnv/AGENTS.md` shall list them.

The program shall land each Phase 2 slice on `main` through a pull request merged by rebase or merge commit after one Reviewer review at its integration step, at most one repair round and a green gate run, with no squash merge, force-push or commit on local `main`.

Every Reviewer packet shall carry OCR in delegation mode (`ocr delegate preview --from <base> --to <head>`, `ocr delegate rule <files>`) and either a Reverify run for any claim about a built APK or `Reverify: not applicable — <reason>`; an OCR or Reverify run that cannot complete shall be recorded as a typed gap with its exact error.

Every slice that changes rendered TV UI shall be reviewed on the real stick before merge: each changed screen and state captured with `adb exec-out screencap -p` at the device's output resolution under `evidence/visual/<slice>/`, judged against the spec and AFC-PR-043/-045, with no account or customer data in captures.

Every defect found during Phase 2 (failing gate or landing, acceptance check, flaky test, review finding) shall be triaged with `bug-hunter-triage` and its fix and review dispatched on the bug-triager routes, with a packet carrying reproduction, origin and escape, product vs test-only classification, a red-then-green regression and a prevention check; a packet that keeps a lane route states `BUG_ROUTE: <reason>`.
The program shall commit no file containing an absolute local home path; plan artifacts and evidence use repository-relative paths or `$HOME` / `<PHASE2_PLAN_WORKTREE>` placeholders.

The program shall obtain a scan-software-supply-chain receipt before first use of each external acquisition (Android SDK command-line tools and platform-tools, the starter repository at its pinned commit, Gradle wrapper and plugin versions, AWS SAM CLI, cfn-lint, Python test dependencies, each pinned GitHub Action) and refuse use on BLOCK or INDETERMINATE.

Every Phase 2 pull request that lands shall add one `CHANGELOG.md` `## [Unreleased]` entry (Keep a Changelog section Added, Changed, Fixed or Removed) naming the change and linking the pull request; the first Phase 2 landing seeds `CHANGELOG.md` when it is absent.

At each technical-wave release checkpoint W1..W5 the program shall prepare a release through the `release-process` skill: version, tag name and release notes drawn from the changelog, with the `[Unreleased]` entries moved under the version heading; it shall publish the release only after the owner authorizes that publication.

When the panel (P2-X04), provider (P2-X03) and notification (P2-X02) spike verdicts have landed, the D1 specification shall be revised to record every landed spike verdict from P2-X01..P2-X07 (plus P2-X11 when it runs), the verdict-selected panel mode and provider routes with every recorded limitation, the aligned model names (`PanelMode.fullScreen`, no `tvApp.player`, AFC-PR-066 allocation) and the Glossary Lifecycle-local design quantities as approved under OD-AFC-05, with a revision row listing the changed sections and linking the pull request and its diff, and `gate.sh spec` shall pass with a byte-identical rebuild.

The technical plan shall define Phase 2 waves in which every slice belongs to exactly one wave, no wave schedules more than impl_agent_cap concurrent implementation agents, and serialization is declared only for dependencies, shared interfaces, write-set overlap, the leases `fire-tv-stick`, `aws-afc-dev`, `live-game-window`, `tv-app-manifest`, `tv-app-gradle`, `backend-template` and `main-landing`, or impl_agent_cap.

After the owner approves this package, the program shall create GitHub milestones M01..M13 in `1wgrumph/amazon-fantasy-companion` whose title, due date (calendar date; the UTC due time is stated in the description) and description (entry criteria, exit criteria, slice list) equal the approved milestone table, and shall record a `gh api` readback that matches it field for field; no milestone is created before approval.

The plan shall state the remaining days to T_deadline and the remaining live windows, schedule each spike before the live window it needs, and present any scope reduction as an owner decision rather than cutting scope silently.

The repository shall contain a README with a product description, fresh-setup instructions for the TV app and the backend (from a clean checkout, using only repository-relative paths and documented owner-supplied inputs), the judge-access route through T_judge_access, the known limitations recorded by the spike verdicts, and the voice/Alexa status (implemented and verified on the device, or not offered).

The program shall produce a demo video plan of at most 2 min 50 s covering the alert → Watch → correct game or channel moment and the lineup panel moment from issue #1 §Judging alignment, naming for each shot its source (on-device capture, owner camera capture, or labeled replay) and the register UIDs it shows; no shot claims behavior that has no passing evidence.

The submission write-up shall describe the implemented Fire TV and AWS Builder integrations from their evidence, state the YouTube TV Fantasy View differentiation (roster scores beside the game there; tune-in alerts and cross-provider Watch here), and discuss the DEC-AFC-SD-036 future direction (AWS-powered analytics viewing on Prime Video; Amazon's NBA rights) with public citations, marked as external context and not product capability.
Every Phase 2 dispatch packet and return shall carry a `developer_feedback` section listing observations with IDs and evidence, or "no new observations" naming the tools exercised.

Before W5 exit the Scribe shall assemble, from `docs/developer-feedback/observations.md`, a per-tool Product Feedback file (used for, what worked well, what needs work, onboarding from zero to hello world, would build again Yes/No and why, AWS services used and how), optional Feature Requests with priority Critical / Important / Nice-to-have, and a sanitized Friction Log with the Devpost entry fields, covering every tool, API, SDK and device used in Phase 2, with no credentials, account details or local paths, and shall check the Product Feedback file and the Friction Log against the official rules current at submission.

The program shall produce a submission checklist listing every owner-only action (OA-1..OA-11 and the §Exclusions owner-only actions) with its due time before T_deadline, and agents shall perform none of those actions.

The submitted APK shall be built from a tagged commit on `main`, its sha256 recorded, and Reverify run on that exact APK for every claim the submission makes about it (minSdk 25, package identity, declared permissions and services), with a Reverify failure or unavailability recorded as a typed gap.

If P2-X01 finds Fire OS 5, an API level below min_sdk, or a stick that cannot run the provider apps, then the program shall stop dependent device slices and raise a class C owner stop; it shall not buy a device or switch platform.
before.Response: Owner decides; device-independent backend and docs work continues.

before.text: If P2-X02 shows no supported heads-up notification over provider playback, then the verdict shall name the exact limitation and the program shall raise a class C owner stop before AFC-PR-015 product code; it shall not substitute a phone screen or a companion-app-only alert silently.
before.Risk (rationale): Fire OS notification behavior over third-party playback is documented only for 2020.
before.Response: Owner decides scope; the rest continues.

before.text: If no supported provider game or channel link exists for a provider, then the resolver and launcher shall report the strongest observed outcome (`searchOpened`, `appHomeOpened`, `appAbsent`, `accessUnknown`, `playbackDenied`) honestly and the verdict shall record the missing interface as an integration gap; no outcome is relabeled `gameOpened`.
before.Risk (rationale): Provider deep-link contracts may be private.
before.Response: Honest outcome; integration gap documented for the write-up.

before.text: If the panel spike fails or reaches spike_panel_max, then the panel shall be built as `PanelMode.fullScreen` (AFC-PR-047) with alerts and Watch still routed to the real provider apps (AFC-PR-048).
before.Risk (rationale): Third-party video composition is not a documented public capability.

before.text: If the ESPN endpoint is unavailable or its contract changes, then ingest shall serve labeled replay fixtures for every affected value (AFC-PR-013) and reject schema-invalid responses without mutation (AFC-PR-064); the ESPN terms question shall be presented to the owner before submission (C3).
before.Risk (rationale): Unofficial JSON can change without notice.

before.text: If Yahoo approval is absent at T_yahoo, then P2-X06 shall record a FAILS verdict for the Yahoo route selecting labeled manual entry, and the backend shall use labeled manual entry as the single active source (AFC-PR-006, -007).
before.Risk (rationale): Yahoo review time is outside our control (Q7 not yet submitted).

before.text: If any AWS action would require a Paid plan, a paid service or a payment method change, then the slice shall stop and raise a class F owner stop; no agent upgrades the account.
before.Risk (rationale): The Free plan may refuse a service or quota.

before.text: If a live window is missed or a game produces no qualifying event, then the slice shall use labeled replay of captured fixtures for repeatability and schedule the live check in the next live window; replay never stands in for live notification or provider behavior evidence.
before.Risk (rationale): Only four live windows remain after approval.
before.Response: Replay for logic; live windows reserved for device evidence.

before.text: If `adb` screencap or screenrecord returns black or blank frames for protected provider video, then the visual evidence shall combine the companion UI capture with window geometry from `dumpsys` and, if OD-AFC-P2-02 = A, an owner camera capture of the screen (OA-9); the demo plan shall mark any owner-filmed shots as owner-filmed and, if OD-AFC-P2-02 = B, shall use companion UI captures only for those shots.
before.Risk (rationale): Provider apps commonly use secure surfaces that screen capture cannot read.
before.Response: Geometry plus owner camera capture under A, companion UI only under B (OD-AFC-P2-02).

before.text: If a selected route reaches a confirmed usage or rate limit, then the Orchestrator shall record the evidence and activate only the next approved fallback of the frozen profile with a class B receipt preserving coverage-assist and Reverify settings, or queue the slice; other errors shall not trigger a route switch.

If Phase 1 slice S09 (gate entrypoint) has not merged when a Phase 2 slice is ready to land, then the slice shall wait for S09 and P2-G01; it shall not land without a green gate run, and development continues on its branch with local test evidence.
before.Risk (rationale): S09 has merged; the Phase 2 product gate extension P2-G01 remains a prerequisite.

before.text: When a secret, account detail, customer data or absolute local path is detected in material bound for the repository, release, video or submission, the program shall block that merge or publication until sanitized, and if exposure has occurred shall record the artifact without reproducing the value and notify the owner for rotation.
before.Risk (rationale): Yahoo tokens, AWS profile names and provider account names can leak into captures and logs.
before.Response: Block and sanitize; rotation is the owner's action.

before.text: If a technical-wave release checkpoint W1..W5 is at risk of missing its due time by more than 12 h, then the Orchestrator shall present the owner a scope-reduction decision using the priority order in §Program plan, not cut scope silently.
before.Risk (rationale): The deadline, device spikes and live windows constrain the schedule; the as-of remaining time is stated in Program plan.

after.text: The backend shall retrieve the customer's leagues, teams, rosters by week, and league scoring settings through a read-only Yahoo Fantasy OAuth connection.
after.Rationale: Yahoo is the lineup/league context source; read-only OAuth bounds access to need.
after.Verification method: Test, backend, AWS Free-plan deployment (SD-005). Positive: roster distinguishes active slots from bench and returns scoring settings. Negative: no write-scope call is attempted and no player eligibility value is used as a starting-slot fact. VCASE-AFC-PR-001.

after.text: The TV app shall persist the customer's selected leagues, teams, starters or specific players, and favorite teams.
after.Rationale: Selections drive monitoring, alerts, and panel content; loss across restart breaks trust.
after.Verification method: Demonstration, system, real stick (SD-001) + backend. Positive: select, restart, selections retained. Negative: no selection silently dropped. VCASE-AFC-PR-002.

after.text: The TV app shall report each supported installed viewing app as installed through platform-permitted detection.
after.Rationale: Provider choice needs true installed-app facts without claiming subscription.
after.Verification method: Demonstration, tv-app, real stick (SD-001). Positive: each installed supported app reported installed. Negative: absent app never reported installed. VCASE-AFC-PR-003.

after.text: The backend shall mark each game's viewing access as verified only from supported provider integration or explicit customer confirmation.
after.Rationale: Honest availability is a judging emphasis; unverified access must never read as verified.
after.Verification method: Test, backend, AWS deployment. Positive: verified marking carries basis integration or confirmation. Negative: installed-app fact alone never yields verified. VCASE-AFC-PR-004.

after.text: The TV app shall apply the customer's review and override to all detected profile information and retained local-market information.
after.Rationale: Detection is fallible; the customer is the final authority on their profile.
after.Verification method: Demonstration, tv-app, real stick (SD-001). Positive: override of a detected app and of local market persists across restart and feed refresh. Negative: refresh never silently discards an override. VCASE-AFC-PR-005.

after.text: When Yahoo approval is absent at T_yahoo (2026-10-16T19:00:00Z), the backend shall accept labeled manual lineup entry built from ESPN rosters as the active lineup source.
after.Rationale: Schedule-proof lineup context without misrepresenting manual data as Yahoo data.
after.Verification method: Test, backend, AWS deployment. Positive: at/after T_yahoo without approval, manual entry activates and is labeled manual. Negative: manual values never presented as Yahoo values. VCASE-AFC-PR-006.

after.text: The backend shall hold exactly one active lineup source from the Yahoo read-only connection or labeled manual entry.
after.Rationale: Two simultaneous sources would fork lineup truth across alerts and panel.
after.Verification method: Test, backend, AWS deployment. Positive: source query returns exactly one active source. Negative: switchover never leaves zero or two active. VCASE-AFC-PR-007.

after.text: The backend shall monitor live NFL game events only for profile-relevant games during customer-enabled viewing periods.
after.Rationale: Relevance and customer control bound noise, cost, and backend load.
after.Verification method: Test, backend, AWS deployment. Positive: game with a selected player or favorite team inside an enabled period is monitored. Negative: irrelevant game, or any game in quiet hours, is not monitored. VCASE-AFC-PR-008.

after.text: The TV app shall record the customer's selected schedule and game-day mode as the monitoring enablement.
after.Rationale: The customer decides when the companion watches.
after.Verification method: Demonstration, system, real stick (SD-001) + backend. Positive: mode change alters the monitored game set per PR-008. Negative: no monitoring outside the recorded enablement. VCASE-AFC-PR-009.

after.text: The TV app shall apply current-viewing-context detection only through supported mechanisms while the customer enables that detection.
after.Rationale: Viewing-context sensing is sensitive and platform-limited; both bounds apply.
after.Verification method: Demonstration, tv-app, real stick (SD-001). Positive: enabled detection uses a documented supported mechanism. Negative: disabled detection yields no viewing-context reads (decisions label profile-assumption per PR-011). VCASE-AFC-PR-010.

after.text: The backend shall label each monitoring decision with its observed-playback or profile-assumption basis.
after.Rationale: Observed state and assumption must never be confused downstream.
after.Verification method: Test, backend, AWS deployment. Positive: every decision record carries exactly one basis label. Negative: no decision ships unlabeled. VCASE-AFC-PR-011.

after.text: The backend shall ingest scores, field position, possession, involved player identifiers, timestamps, and scoring corrections from ESPN's unofficial public JSON.
after.Rationale: Owner-selected live feed; corrections and timestamps ground freshness and panel truth.
after.Verification method: Test, backend, AWS deployment. Positive: each listed field lands in the event cache. Negative: schema-invalid response handled per PR-064, never partially stored. VCASE-AFC-PR-012.

after.text: When the ESPN endpoint is unavailable or its contract changes, the backend shall substitute labeled replay fixtures for live events on every affected value.
after.Rationale: Repeatability and outage survival without ever faking live access.
after.Verification method: Test, backend, AWS deployment with fixtures. Positive: outage run marks every affected value replay. Negative: no substituted value presented as live. VCASE-AFC-PR-013.

after.text: The backend shall emit alerts for red-zone opportunities, player scores, and close games matching the customer's fantasy selections and alert-type settings.
after.Rationale: The core personalized value: this event matters to this customer.
after.Verification method: Test, backend, AWS deployment. Positive: each of the three types fires for a matching selection. Negative: non-matching event, or matching event of a disabled type, emits nothing; red zone means inside the 20-yard line; close_game_margin (DEC-AFC-SD-035, P1) is within 8 points in the 4th quarter or overtime. VCASE-AFC-PR-014. Alert text claims no player-level inference per PR-028.

after.text: While heads-up presentation is selected, the TV app shall present each alert as a heads-up notification with Watch and Dismiss actions during third-party viewing-app playback.
after.Rationale: The standout moment: brief alert over playback with a direct Watch path.
after.Verification method: Demonstration, system, real stick (SD-001); evidence under evidence/visual/ (SD-024). Positive: provider playback continues while the alert shows Watch/Dismiss. Negative: no companion-app foregrounding, and no heads-up while panel-only presentation is selected. VCASE-AFC-PR-015.

after.text: The backend shall emit alerts only for customer-enabled alert types.
after.Rationale: Per-type control is the primary noise control.
after.Verification method: Test, system, backend + settings UI. Positive: enabled type fires on matching event. Negative: disabled type fires on nothing. VCASE-AFC-PR-016.

after.text: The backend shall emit no more alerts than the customer's frequency setting permits.
after.Rationale: Frequency caps keep the companion welcome during simultaneous Sunday games.
after.Verification method: Test, system, backend + settings UI. Positive: restrictive setting yields fewer alerts than permissive for an identical event stream. Negative: no alert beyond the setting on any run. VCASE-AFC-PR-017.

after.text: The backend shall suppress alerts during the customer's quiet hours.
after.Rationale: Silence when the customer demands silence.
after.Verification method: Test, system, backend + settings UI. Positive: triggering event inside quiet hours emits nothing. Negative: no quiet-hours alert on any run. VCASE-AFC-PR-018.

after.text: The backend shall emit alerts only during the customer's game-day periods.
after.Rationale: Alerts belong to game time, not all time.
after.Verification method: Test, system, backend + settings UI. Positive: triggering event inside a game-day period emits (subject to other filters). Negative: nothing emits outside game-day periods. VCASE-AFC-PR-019.

after.text: The backend shall delay each alert by the customer's spoiler delay.
after.Rationale: Customers behind live play must not be spoiled by their own companion.
after.Verification method: Test, backend, AWS deployment. Positive: delivery timestamp minus event timestamp is at least the set delay. Negative: no alert delivered early. VCASE-AFC-PR-020.

after.text: The TV app shall render each alert in the customer's chosen notification presentation.
after.Rationale: Presentation choice balances intrusiveness and awareness per customer.
after.Verification method: Demonstration, tv-app, real stick (SD-001). Positive: each offered presentation renders as chosen. Negative: panel-only choice shows no heads-up. VCASE-AFC-PR-021.

after.text: The TV app shall announce alerts by voice only while the customer enables voice announcements over an implemented and verified voice route.
after.Rationale: Voice is intrusive and platform-conditional; both gates apply.
after.Verification method: Demonstration, tv-app, real stick (SD-001). Positive: enabled announcements speak over the verified route. Negative: no voice when disabled or when the route is unverified. VCASE-AFC-PR-022.

after.text: The backend shall attach excitement commentary to an alert only at or below the customer's excitement level with every named entity grounded in the triggering event data.
after.Rationale: Optional flavor that can never invent events, scores, or player identity.
after.Verification method: Test, backend, AWS deployment. Positive: every named entity in commentary appears in the triggering event data. Negative: level off attaches nothing, and no model output determines an event, score, or player identity; level change alters commentary for an identical event; excitement_levels (DEC-AFC-SD-035, P2) are Off / Mild / Hype. VCASE-AFC-PR-023.

after.text: The backend shall resolve player and event identifiers across providers to single identities.
after.Rationale: Yahoo, ESPN, and provider ids must converge or matching produces false alerts.
after.Verification method: Test, backend, AWS deployment. Positive: same player/event across sources resolves to one identity. Negative: no two identities for one entity, no merged distinct entities. VCASE-AFC-PR-024.

after.text: The backend shall emit at most one alert per resolved event.
after.Rationale: Duplicate deliveries for one event destroy trust in the companion.
after.Verification method: Test, backend, AWS deployment. Positive: repeated retrieval of an unchanged event emits nothing further. Negative: no second alert for one resolved event. VCASE-AFC-PR-025.

after.text: The backend shall propagate each scoring correction to previously emitted alerts and panel state.
after.Rationale: Stale wrong scores must be repaired everywhere the customer saw them.
after.Verification method: Test, system, AWS deployment. Positive: correction updates the alert record and the panel value. Negative: no corrected fact left stale in either surface. VCASE-AFC-PR-026.

after.text: Each alert shall carry the verified player and matchup context that triggered it.
after.Rationale: The customer must see why this event matters to them.
after.Verification method: Demonstration, system, real stick (SD-001) + backend. Positive: alert shows the triggering player and matchup from lineup and feed data. Negative: no alert without its triggering context. VCASE-AFC-PR-027.

after.text: The system shall withhold any claim that a team red-zone entry proves a particular player is on the field or will score.
after.Rationale: The precise over-claim the owner forbade.
after.Verification method: Test, system, backend + TV surfaces. Positive: red-zone alert text makes only team-level claims. Negative: any player-on-field or will-score claim from a red-zone entry fails. VCASE-AFC-PR-028.

after.text: The backend shall resolve each alerted event to an available provider and channel from the customer's installed apps, verified subscriptions, local market, and provider preference.
after.Rationale: Correct game/channel routing is the handoff half of the standout moment. Phase 2 link-contract spike order per SD-035 (Q5): Prime Video (TNF), ESPN app, DirecTV Stream app, YouTube TV.
after.Verification method: Test, backend, AWS deployment. Positive: resolution output names provider and channel with inputs recorded; local-broadcast games (CBS/FOX/NBC) resolve to the channel plus a carrying provider app when one is available. Negative: no resolution from installed-app fact alone; no deep link when no carrying app is available. VCASE-AFC-PR-029.

after.text: The TV app shall open the resolved game or channel through a supported provider launch URI or intent upon the customer's Watch action.
after.Rationale: Watch must reach the game, not merely the provider home screen.
after.Verification method: Demonstration, system, real stick (SD-001); evidence under evidence/visual/ (SD-024). Positive: correct game/channel opens. Negative: app-home landing does not satisfy; app launch alone does not satisfy. VCASE-AFC-PR-030.

after.text: The TV app shall report each routing outcome as exactly one of game opened, search or details opened, app home opened, app absent, access unknown, or playback denied.
after.Rationale: Explicit outcomes make partial success visible instead of silently degraded.
after.Verification method: Demonstration, tv-app, real stick (SD-001). Positive: each attempted route reports exactly one enum value. Negative: no silent outcome, no invented value. VCASE-AFC-PR-031.

after.text: The system shall mark game access it cannot verify as unknown.
after.Rationale: The explicit unknown-access behavior: doubt is displayed, never smoothed over.
after.Verification method: Test, system, backend + TV surfaces. Positive: unverifiable access reads unknown on alerts, Watch routing, and panel. Negative: no unverified access reads verified or included. VCASE-AFC-PR-032.

after.text: The system shall withhold any promise that a game is included merely because the provider app is installed.
after.Rationale: The companion must never sell access it cannot confirm.
after.Verification method: Test, system, backend + TV surfaces. Positive: installed-without-verified-subscription reads unknown per PR-032. Negative: any inclusion promise from install fact alone fails. VCASE-AFC-PR-033.

after.text: The backend shall choose among available services by the customer's provider preference.
after.Rationale: The customer decides which of their services wins a contested game.
after.Verification method: Test, system, backend + settings UI. Positive: preference change reroutes a contested game. Negative: no available-service choice contradicts the recorded preference. VCASE-AFC-PR-034.

after.text: The TV app shall honor the customer's switching-confirmation setting for every viewing switch.
after.Rationale: Unconfirmed channel switches would hijack the customer's viewing.
after.Verification method: Demonstration, system, real stick (SD-001). Positive: confirmation-required setting blocks switching until confirmed. Negative: no automatic switch unless explicitly configured and supported. VCASE-AFC-PR-035.

after.text: The TV app shall offer Alexa-assisted tuning for the resolved game or channel only when the customer enables voice control over an implemented and verified Alexa route.
after.Rationale: Alexa is an additional voice route, never an assumed capability.
after.Verification method: Demonstration, tv-app, real stick (SD-001). Positive: enabled control over a verified route offers tuning. Negative: no Alexa offer when disabled or the route is unverified. VCASE-AFC-PR-036.

after.text: The system shall use detection data and profile-based personalization only while the customer opts in to detection and personalization.
after.Rationale: The master switch for sensing and personalization.
after.Verification method: Test, system, backend + settings UI. Positive: opt-out yields monitoring without detection data or personalization. Negative: no detection-basis decision while opted out (labels per PR-011). VCASE-AFC-PR-037.

after.text: The backend shall link the TV app to the customer account through a device code the customer completes on a phone or browser.
after.Rationale: TV-friendly linking without typing credentials on the stick.
after.Verification method: Demonstration, system, real stick + phone/browser page. Positive: code entry on phone/browser links the TV app. Negative: no link completes without the customer's code action. VCASE-AFC-PR-038.

after.text: The TV app shall display the selected fantasy team's lineup with each player's fantasy points and game status and the team total and progress under the league's scoring context.
after.Rationale: The panel's core content: my players, my points, my progress.
after.Verification method: Demonstration, system, real stick (SD-001) + backend; evidence under evidence/visual/ (SD-024). Positive: lineup, points, statuses, and total match the Yahoo league context (or PR-065 selected preset table for manual). Negative: no value shown without its scoring basis. VCASE-AFC-PR-039.

after.text: The TV app shall label each unavailable or stale panel value as unavailable or stale.
after.Rationale: The explicit stale-data behavior: age and absence are visible.
after.Verification method: Demonstration, tv-app, real stick (SD-001). Positive: withheld feed and missing value produce stale and unavailable labels. Negative: no silently old or silently missing value; stale_after is 60 seconds (DEC-AFC-SD-035, P3). VCASE-AFC-PR-040.

after.text: The TV app shall fit the broadcast video into the screen area remaining beside the right-side lineup panel while preserving broadcast aspect ratio.
after.Rationale: The panel supplements viewing; it must never cover or crop the broadcast.
after.Verification method: Demonstration, tv-app, real stick (SD-001); evidence under evidence/visual/ (SD-024). Positive: simultaneous panel and video with no overlap and preserved aspect (dimension-compared capture). Negative: any overlap or crop fails. VCASE-AFC-PR-041.

after.text: The TV app shall switch panel visibility and the followed team and league from TV remote input.
after.Rationale: Core panel controls operable from the couch.
after.Verification method: Demonstration, tv-app, real stick (SD-001); evidence under evidence/visual/ (SD-024). Positive: remote toggles visibility and changes team/league. Negative: no panel control requires another input device. VCASE-AFC-PR-042.

after.text: The lineup panel shall accept all panel operations from TV remote input.
after.Rationale: Full panel use without leaving the couch.
after.Verification method: Demonstration, tv-app, real stick (SD-001); evidence under evidence/visual/ (SD-024). Positive: every focusable element reachable with a visible focus indicator. Negative: no remote-dead operation. VCASE-AFC-PR-043.

after.text: The lineup panel shall reflect the customer's team, league, and display settings.
after.Rationale: The panel is a view of the customer's settings, not a second configuration.
after.Verification method: Test, system, backend + TV panel. Positive: settings change appears on the panel. Negative: no panel content contradicts recorded settings. VCASE-AFC-PR-044.

after.text: The lineup panel shall present lineup text the owner accepts as legible from the couch on the target device, with body text at least 24 px and scores at least 32 px at 1080p.
after.Rationale: Couch legibility is judged by the owner on the real target, with a numeric floor per SD-035 (Q3).
after.Verification method: Demonstration, tv-app, real stick (SD-001). Positive: owner accepts lineup text as couch-legible in the demonstration and body text measures at least 24 px with scores at least 32 px at 1080p. Negative: owner rejection or under-size text fails the case. VCASE-AFC-PR-045.
after.Sources: #1 right-side panel (legible from the couch); SD-035 (Q3)

after.text: The system shall hold lineup panel state consistent with alerts across starter changes and scoring corrections.
after.Rationale: Panel and alerts are two views of one truth.
after.Verification method: Test, system, AWS deployment. Positive: starter change and correction reach both surfaces with identical corrected facts. Negative: no fact present in one surface and contradicted in the other (suppressed alerts do not break fact agreement; hidden panel refreshes on show). VCASE-AFC-PR-046.

after.text: When the panel-beside-provider-video spike fails or exceeds 24 hours from first app install, the TV app shall present the lineup panel as a full screen in the companion app.
after.Rationale: No Mode A footage per owner decision (SD-035, Q4): the product is alerts + Watch, and the panel fallback is a full screen in our own app.
after.Verification method: Demonstration, tv-app, real stick (SD-001); evidence under evidence/visual/ (SD-024). Positive: full-screen lineup panel in the companion app. Negative: no stand-in video, no provider video claimed, and no silent substitution of phone screen, app-switch dashboard, or covering panel. VCASE-AFC-PR-047.

after.text: Before any product slice depends on a device, provider, feed, lineup or voice route, the program shall run the spike for that route on the real target and land `spikes/<sp>/VERDICT.md` stating the verdict, the exact route tried, the observed result with evidence paths, the conditional it triggers (C1, C2, C5, C6, C8) and the register UIDs it unblocks.

The panel-beside-provider-video spike shall return its verdict within spike_panel_max of the first app install on the stick (recorded by P2-X01), and the verdict shall select `PanelMode.modeB` only with on-device evidence of simultaneous provider video and panel with no overlap or crop; otherwise it shall select `PanelMode.fullScreen` (AFC-PR-047).

The provider-link spike shall try Prime Video (TNF), ESPN app, DirecTV Stream app and YouTube TV in that order plus local-broadcast channel display, and shall record for each provider the package identity, the supported launch URI or intent with its documentation source, the observed routing outcome from the six-value vocabulary, and whether game arrival was observed; it shall invent no URI format.

The gate entrypoint `tools/ci/gate.sh` shall gain the areas `tvapp` (Gradle unit tests, Android lint and debug assemble under `tv-app/`) and `backend` (pytest and SAM template validation under `backend/`), invoked by the same local hooks and Actions workflow with path filters, stable check names and pinned actions per AC-AFC-CI-02; each area shall exit non-zero on any failing check, shall record a missing tool as a typed gap with its exact error and exit non-zero, and shall report `PASS` with the detail `no <dir>/ tree` only when its directory does not exist.
after.Source: DEC-AFC-SD-023 (Phase 2 adds product areas), Phase 1 AC-AFC-CI-01/02, CONTRACT-AFC-GATE

after.text: The Vnv guidance tree shall gain `docs/vnv/tv-app/AGENTS.md`, `docs/vnv/backend/AGENTS.md` and `docs/vnv/device-integration/AGENTS.md`, each naming Scope, Tools, Review Focus and findings target, and the index `docs/vnv/AGENTS.md` shall list them.

The program shall land each Phase 2 slice on `main` through a pull request merged by rebase or merge commit after one Reviewer review at its integration step, at most one repair round and a green gate run, with no squash merge, force-push or commit on local `main`.

Every Reviewer packet shall carry OCR in delegation mode (`ocr delegate preview --from <base> --to <head>`, `ocr delegate rule <files>`) and either a Reverify run for any claim about a built APK or `Reverify: not applicable — <reason>`; an OCR or Reverify run that cannot complete shall be recorded as a typed gap with its exact error.

Every slice that changes rendered TV UI shall be reviewed on the real stick before merge: each changed screen and state captured with `adb exec-out screencap -p` at the device's output resolution under `evidence/visual/<slice>/`, judged against the spec and AFC-PR-043/-045, with no account or customer data in captures.

Every defect found during Phase 2 (failing gate or landing, acceptance check, flaky test, review finding) shall be triaged with `bug-hunter-triage` and its fix and review dispatched on the bug-triager routes, with a packet carrying reproduction, origin and escape, product vs test-only classification, a red-then-green regression and a prevention check; a packet that keeps a lane route states `BUG_ROUTE: <reason>`.
The program shall commit no file containing an absolute local home path; plan artifacts and evidence use repository-relative paths or `$HOME` / `<PHASE2_PLAN_WORKTREE>` placeholders.

The program shall obtain a scan-software-supply-chain receipt before first use of each external acquisition (Android SDK command-line tools and platform-tools, the starter repository at its pinned commit, Gradle wrapper and plugin versions, AWS SAM CLI, cfn-lint, Python test dependencies, each pinned GitHub Action) and refuse use on BLOCK or INDETERMINATE.

Every Phase 2 pull request that lands shall add one `CHANGELOG.md` `## [Unreleased]` entry (Keep a Changelog section Added, Changed, Fixed or Removed) naming the change and linking the pull request; the first Phase 2 landing seeds `CHANGELOG.md` when it is absent.

At each technical-wave release checkpoint W1..W5 the program shall prepare a release through the `release-process` skill: version, tag name and release notes drawn from the changelog, with the `[Unreleased]` entries moved under the version heading; it shall publish the release only after the owner authorizes that publication.

When the panel (P2-X04), provider (P2-X03) and notification (P2-X02) spike verdicts have landed, the D1 specification shall be revised to record every landed spike verdict from P2-X01..P2-X07 (plus P2-X11 when it runs), the verdict-selected panel mode and provider routes with every recorded limitation, the aligned model names (`PanelMode.fullScreen`, no `tvApp.player`, AFC-PR-066 allocation) and the Glossary Lifecycle-local design quantities as approved under OD-AFC-05, with a revision row listing the changed sections and linking the pull request and its diff, and `gate.sh spec` shall pass with a byte-identical rebuild.

The technical plan shall define Phase 2 waves in which every slice belongs to exactly one wave, no wave schedules more than impl_agent_cap concurrent implementation agents, and serialization is declared only for dependencies, shared interfaces, write-set overlap, the leases `fire-tv-stick`, `aws-afc-dev`, `live-game-window`, `tv-app-manifest`, `tv-app-gradle`, `backend-template` and `main-landing`, or impl_agent_cap.

After the owner approves this package, the program shall create GitHub milestones M01..M13 in `1wgrumph/amazon-fantasy-companion` whose title, due date (calendar date; the UTC due time is stated in the description) and description (entry criteria, exit criteria, issues in order) equal the approved table `GitHub milestones in order (D3; create only after approval)`, and shall record a `gh api` readback that matches it field for field; no milestone is created before approval.

The plan shall state the remaining days to T_deadline and the remaining live windows, schedule each spike before the live window it needs, and present any scope reduction as an owner decision rather than cutting scope silently.

The repository shall contain a README with a product description, fresh-setup instructions for the TV app and the backend (from a clean checkout, using only repository-relative paths and documented owner-supplied inputs), the judge-access route through T_judge_access, the known limitations recorded by the spike verdicts, and the voice/Alexa status (implemented and verified on the device, or not offered).

The program shall produce a demo video plan of at most 2 min 50 s covering the alert → Watch → correct game or channel moment and the lineup panel moment from issue #1 §Judging alignment, naming for each shot its source (on-device capture, owner camera capture, or labeled replay) and the register UIDs it shows; no shot claims behavior that has no passing evidence.

The submission write-up shall describe the implemented Fire TV and AWS Builder integrations from their evidence, state the YouTube TV Fantasy View differentiation (roster scores beside the game there; tune-in alerts and cross-provider Watch here), and discuss the DEC-AFC-SD-036 future direction (AWS-powered analytics viewing on Prime Video; Amazon's NBA rights) with public citations, marked as external context and not product capability.
Every Phase 2 dispatch packet and return shall carry a `developer_feedback` section listing observations with IDs and evidence, or "no new observations" naming the tools exercised.

Before W5 exit the Scribe shall assemble, from `docs/developer-feedback/observations.md`, a per-tool Product Feedback file (used for, what worked well, what needs work, onboarding from zero to hello world, would build again Yes/No and why, AWS services used and how), optional Feature Requests with priority Critical / Important / Nice-to-have, and a sanitized Friction Log with the Devpost entry fields, covering every tool, API, SDK and device used in Phase 2, with no credentials, account details or local paths, and shall check the Product Feedback file and the Friction Log against the official rules current at submission.

The program shall produce a submission checklist listing every owner-only action (OA-1..OA-11 and the §Exclusions owner-only actions) with its due time before T_deadline, and agents shall perform none of those actions.

The submitted APK shall be built from a tagged commit on `main`, its sha256 recorded, and Reverify run on that exact APK for every claim the submission makes about it (minSdk 25, package identity, declared permissions and services), with a Reverify failure or unavailability recorded as a typed gap.

If P2-X01 finds Fire OS 5, an API level below min_sdk, or a stick that cannot run the provider apps, then the program shall stop dependent device slices and raise a class C owner stop; it shall not buy a device or switch platform.
after.Response: Owner decides; device-independent backend and docs work continues.

after.text: If P2-X02 shows no supported heads-up notification over provider playback, then the verdict shall name the exact limitation and the program shall raise a class C owner stop before AFC-PR-015 product code; it shall not substitute a phone screen or a companion-app-only alert silently.
after.Risk (rationale): Fire OS notification behavior over third-party playback is documented only for 2020.
after.Response: Owner decides scope; the rest continues.

after.text: If no supported provider game or channel link exists for a provider, then the resolver and launcher shall report the strongest observed outcome (`searchOpened`, `appHomeOpened`, `appAbsent`, `accessUnknown`, `playbackDenied`) honestly and the verdict shall record the missing interface as an integration gap; no outcome is relabeled `gameOpened`.
after.Risk (rationale): Provider deep-link contracts may be private.
after.Response: Honest outcome; integration gap documented for the write-up.

after.text: If the panel spike fails or reaches spike_panel_max, then the panel shall be built as `PanelMode.fullScreen` (AFC-PR-047) with alerts and Watch still routed to the real provider apps (AFC-PR-048).
after.Risk (rationale): Third-party video composition is not a documented public capability.

after.text: If the ESPN endpoint is unavailable or its contract changes, then ingest shall serve labeled replay fixtures for every affected value (AFC-PR-013) and reject schema-invalid responses without mutation (AFC-PR-064); the ESPN terms question shall be presented to the owner before submission (C3).
after.Risk (rationale): Unofficial JSON can change without notice.

after.text: If Yahoo approval is absent at T_yahoo, then P2-X06 shall record a FAILS verdict for the Yahoo route selecting labeled manual entry, and the backend shall use labeled manual entry as the single active source (AFC-PR-006, -007).
after.Risk (rationale): Yahoo review time is outside our control (Q7 not yet submitted).

after.text: If any AWS action would require a Paid plan, a paid service or a payment method change, then the slice shall stop and raise a class F owner stop; no agent upgrades the account.
after.Risk (rationale): The Free plan may refuse a service or quota.

after.text: If a live window is missed or a game produces no qualifying event, then the slice shall use labeled replay of captured fixtures for repeatability and schedule the live check in the next live window; replay never stands in for live notification or provider behavior evidence.
after.Risk (rationale): Only four live windows remain after approval.
after.Response: Replay for logic; live windows reserved for device evidence.

after.text: If `adb` screencap or screenrecord returns black or blank frames for protected provider video, then the visual evidence shall combine the companion UI capture with window geometry from `dumpsys` and, if OD-AFC-P2-02 = A, an owner camera capture of the screen (OA-9); the demo plan shall mark any owner-filmed shots as owner-filmed and, if OD-AFC-P2-02 = B, shall use companion UI captures only for those shots.
after.Risk (rationale): Provider apps commonly use secure surfaces that screen capture cannot read.
after.Response: Geometry plus owner camera capture under A, companion UI only under B (OD-AFC-P2-02).

after.text: If a selected route reaches a confirmed usage or rate limit, then the Orchestrator shall record the evidence and activate only the next approved fallback of the frozen profile with a class B receipt preserving coverage-assist and Reverify settings, or queue the slice; other errors shall not trigger a route switch.

If Phase 1 slice S09 (gate entrypoint) has not merged when a Phase 2 slice is ready to land, then the slice shall wait for S09 and P2-G01; it shall not land without a green gate run, and development continues on its branch with local test evidence.
after.Risk (rationale): S09 has merged; the Phase 2 product gate extension P2-G01 remains a prerequisite.

after.text: When a secret, account detail, customer data or absolute local path is detected in material bound for the repository, release, video or submission, the program shall block that merge or publication until sanitized, and if exposure has occurred shall record the artifact without reproducing the value and notify the owner for rotation.
after.Risk (rationale): Yahoo tokens, AWS profile names and provider account names can leak into captures and logs.
after.Response: Block and sanitize; rotation is the owner's action.

after.text: If a technical-wave release checkpoint W1..W5 is at risk of missing its due time by more than 12 h, then the Orchestrator shall present the owner a scope-reduction decision using the priority order in §Program plan, not cut scope silently.
after.Risk (rationale): The deadline, device spikes and live windows constrain the schedule; the as-of remaining time is stated in Program plan.
